messages:
sara (People Ops): Quick Q — our retirement plan vendor is switching to Meridian on May 3. Does anyone know how that affects incoming rollovers/in-plan Roth conversions during the blackout?
ben (Payroll): Good question. Payroll's cutoff for deferrals that month is Apr 28 23:59 PT. Any changes after that go to the new mapping and may not reflect until next cycle. We'll need to confirm employee ID mapping with the vendor.
nate (Benefits Ops): Vendor told us there's a 48–72hr maintenance window May 3–5 where account portals and some transfers will be paused. Contributions should still post but allocations may be queued. Link: https://vendor.example.com/migration (internal doc)
emma (People Ops): So if someone initiates an incoming rollover Apr 30, will the transfer be accepted/processed? Also — in-plan Roth conversions: allowed or paused during migration?
ben (Payroll): Rollover initiations submitted to the old provider by EOD Apr 30 should be accepted, but final posting could be delayed. In-plan Roth conversions require provider-side processing — vendor confirmed conversions will be paused during the blackout. Recommend employees defer conversions until May 6.
jamal (Legal): From compliance side we need an audit trail: record the initiation date and the vendor transfer date. Also draft a short notice to employees about timing and who to contact for questions.
sara (People Ops): Draft notice plan: 1) payroll cutoff for deferral/changes, 2) rollover initiation cutoff, 3) in-plan Roth conversions paused, 4) how to request manual exceptions. I'll draft and share for review.
emma (People Ops): :thumbsup: Can we get a manager-facing one-liner + an employee FAQ snippet for common asks (loans, rollovers, beneficiary updates)?
ben (Payroll): Yes — sample payroll note we can paste into the notice:

``
Payroll cutoff: Apr 28 23:59 PT
Submit rollover initiation to current provider by Apr 30
In-plan Roth conversions paused May 3–5; please wait until May 6 to convert
If you need an exception, email benefits@redwood.com with subject: Migration Exception
``

sara (People Ops): Also flag accounts with active distributions (retirees) — those might need manual handling. @jamal can you confirm whether distributions will continue uninterrupted?
jamal (Legal): Will check. Also confirming whether outstanding loans will continue to amortize during the window or if payments will queue. Vendor response pending.
vendorbot (Benefits Vendor): Automated notice: migration maintenance window 2026-05-03T02:00Z to 2026-05-05T08:00Z. Customer support available but some account updates may be queued.
emma (People Ops): OK let's get the employee notice out tomorrow morning. Sara, can you add a short FAQ item: HSA/FSA impact? My read: HSA contributions unaffected; FSA elections are unrelated.
sara (People Ops): Confirmed — HSA contributions route through payroll and are unaffected by the retirement vendor migration. FSA admin is separate. Draft notice ready, sending for review in ~30m.
ben (Payroll): One more payroll ops note: catch-up contributions (50+) are processed as deferrals. Make sure payroll maps the new plan code for those deferrals. We'll run a dry‑run payroll file on Apr 25 to verify mapping.
emma (People Ops): Great — schedule dry-run and confirm results by Apr 27. I'll create an Asana task and tag payroll + benefits.
sara (People Ops): Perfect. I'll post employee notice and tag payroll at 8:00 AM PT tomorrow. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround!
